assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuinely new observational window: a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice that opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos. It is instrument-driven physics of the kind I value, and it addresses the origin of cosmic rays.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit names only Francis Halzen, who conceived and drove IceCube. A fair prize configuration is possible with him alone, but a large collaboration built the detector and made the discovery, so the committee would have to justify a single-person award or consider unlisted contributors, which this candidate does not allow.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established, and later source evidence (TXS 0506+056 coincidence, NGC 1068, Galactic-plane neutrinos) has been reported. The source-identification picture is still developing, but the core discovery looks stable and independently supported, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the individual-credit question as workable given the collaboration scale.
How much weight the still-emerging source associations should carry versus the 2013 diffuse-flux discovery.
I have not independently verified the current significance of the NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and are the leading platform for redefining the second, for relativistic geodesy and for tests of fundamental constants. This is an instrument and measurement achievement with clear, lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept and built the first realisations; Ye drove the accuracy and stability records. Two laureates fit cleanly. Others (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto, and ion-clock groups) are outside the supplied credit, and the relation to the 2005 and 2012 prizes needs care.
assessment.maturity: Many independent labs now operate lattice clocks and agree at the 1e-18 level. The redefinition of the second has not yet happened, but the technology is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier frequency-comb (2005) and ion-clock (2012) recognition.
Whether recognition should wait for the redefinition of the SI second.
Atomic physics is outside my own expertise, so I would lean on colleagues for the relative priority of Katori and Ye.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics is the architecture behind most superconducting quantum processors and a platform for strong light-matter coupling and quantum-limited readout. It is a clear technique with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed and demonstrated the architecture, and Wallraff gave the first strong-coupling demonstration. The supplied credit has four names, so the committee must choose three and would leave out one decisive contributor.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across many groups and now industrial scale. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits touches the same field, so timing and the overlap are open questions.
uncertainties: Choosing three of four when Wallraff's experimental demonstration is as decisive as the theory.
Overlap with the 2025 prize.
This is outside my core expertise and I would rely on colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of magic-angle flat bands followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened the field of moire quantum materials. Originality and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery, which gives a natural theory-plus-experiment split. Other groups (Cao, Dean, Efetov, Young, Yazdani and others) contributed key follow-on work and are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: The discovery dates from 2018 and has been reproduced widely, but the origin of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated. This may be early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved.
Reproducibility and sample-dependence concerns in the early period.
Condensed matter is outside my own expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetars are a new class of neutron star powered by magnetic fields near 1e15 G. The theory predicted them and X-ray and gamma-ray observations of soft gamma repeaters confirmed them. It links extreme physics to high-energy instruments, which is the area I know best.
assessment.attribution: Duncan and Thompson made the theoretical prediction in 1992, and Kouveliotou led the observational confirmation in 1998, including the SGR 1806-20 period derivative. The theory-plus-observation split is natural, though the Paczynski and Usov contributions and Woods and Hurley's observational role may be raised.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many observations, including the 2004 giant flare and the 2020 fast radio burst from SGR 1935+2154. The interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards this as fundamental physics rather than astrophysics.
Unresolved questions over the full credit for prior theory and for the observational discovery.
I have not verified the finer points of the priority history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ATLAS and CMS made the Higgs discovery possible, and the detector design and construction were a feat of instrumentation. This kind of recognition for detector builders fits my own view of what matters, though the discovery itself has already been honoured.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee led the conception and early leadership of the experiments, but a Nobel prize for several thousand people's work with three spokespersons is hard to defend as showing decisive individual contributions. Other designers and later spokespersons are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed by two independent experiments. Timeliness is not an issue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would give a detector-focused prize after the 2013 Higgs prize.
Fairness of selecting three leaders from very large collaborations.
Nobel statutes concern discoveries and inventions, and the committee would need to decide whether this is an invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry underlies precision tests of gravity, gravimetry, inertial navigation and fundamental-constant measurements. It is a new measurement technique with concrete application, and it also makes cold-atom tests of fundamental physics possible.
assessment.attribution: Bordé, Pritchard and Kasevich and Chu are all central. Chu already received the 1997 prize for laser cooling, and Chu's role in atom interferometry is not in the supplied credit, which leaves a possible gap in fairness. The three listed names can support a configuration but not all contributors are in the list.
assessment.maturity: The technique is well established across many labs. Still, the biggest claimed applications, such as gravitational wave detection and dark-matter searches, are not yet realised.
uncertainties: Chu's earlier prize and unlisted role.
Whether the impact is yet commensurate with a Nobel prize or still prospective.
Atomic physics is outside my own expertise.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Measuring theta-13 through reactor antineutrino disappearance with Daya Bay and RENO (and Double Chooz) was a precision experiment that completed the mixing matrix and opened the way to leptonic CP-violation searches. It is solid detector-driven experimental physics, though a step beyond the 2015 oscillation discovery rather than a new discovery.
assessment.attribution: Wang and Luk led Daya Bay, and Kim led RENO. Double Chooz and T2K (which first indicated nonzero theta-13 from appearance) are not in the supplied credit, so the configuration leaves out parallel claims.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by several experiments and now a standard parameter in global fits. Timeliness is fine.
uncertainties: Competing claims by Double Chooz and T2K.
Whether the committee sees this as a sufficiently distinct discovery after the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize.
Dividing credit between two reactor collaborations.
